hero.title: Akaya Labs
hero.tagline: A software studio. Web, mobile, custom — end to end, all under one roof.
hero.intro: Akaya Labs is a one-person software studio in Rize, Türkiye, run by Ahmet Karaca. It ships its own apps and takes on a few client projects a year. Design, code and release are all done by the same person.

capabilities.title: From idea to launch — every layer, one studio.

site.title: Corporate sites and product pages
site.body: Corporate websites, product landing pages, content and blog sites — from design to launch.

ecommerce.title: Online stores and payment infrastructure
ecommerce.body: Online store setup, payment gateway integration, inventory and order management — ready for Turkish and international markets.

app.title: Dashboards and B2B systems
app.body: Admin panels, customer portals, multi-tenant SaaS and bespoke B2B applications.

mobile.title: iOS and Android
mobile.body: Mobile apps for the App Store and Play Store, built from one codebase.

systems.title: CRM, ERP, scheduling, membership
systems.body: Corporate software solutions for customer relationships, resource planning, scheduling and membership — bespoke for your operations.

desktop.title: macOS and Windows
desktop.body: macOS menu bar utilities, Windows desktop apps and system tools, distributed through the App Store or as signed downloads.

process.title: From first conversation to live release — every step transparent.
process.subtitle: Every project runs on an agreed roadmap. Out-of-scope changes and extra costs need written approval first.

discovery.title: First conversation
discovery.body: We turn your idea, goals and scope into a clear roadmap. No commitment required.

plan.title: Design and technical plan
plan.body: Interface design, architectural decisions and technology choices. We don't start writing code without an approved plan.

build.title: Build and test
build.body: Delivery in stages, with observability and quality control alongside. Every milestone ships with a live preview.

launch.title: Launch and support
launch.body: Production setup, handover and training. The channel stays open for maintenance and new features after launch.

why.title: In a one-person studio, work never changes hands.

single_team.title: One developer, one point of accountability
single_team.body: Design, frontend, backend and mobile are not split between people. One person does them all. The limit is equally plain: only a few projects run at once.

ownership.title: The same person after delivery
ownership.body: Maintenance and change requests go to the person who wrote the product. There is no other team to hand them to.

long_term.title: Long-term support
long_term.body: Delivery isn't the end. The channel stays open for maintenance, scaling and new features — retainer or project-based.

engagement.title: We work on a project basis or via retainer.
engagement.body: A few client projects are taken on each year. It starts with an introductory call and, if there's a fit, scope and timeline are agreed in writing.

partners.subtitle: The tools we design, build and ship our products with.

closing.title: Have a project in mind?
closing.body: Akaya Labs takes on a few client projects a year. If you are planning a SaaS, a mobile product or a focused internal tool, write a few lines; you will hear back within 1–2 business days.

products.title: Products
products.subtitle: {total} products under one roof, {live} of them live. Most are our own brands; one belongs to a client.
products.intro: Akaya Labs' own apps and one client project. All of them designed and built by Ahmet Karaca.

coredence.name: Coredence
coredence.blurb: One memory for all your AI assistants. It reads your notes, chats and code and ties every memory to the traces it grew from. Claude Code, Cursor and VS Code read it directly; ChatGPT gets it as text you paste. Runs on macOS and Windows, and the memory stays on your computer.

stoneye.name: Stoneye
stoneye.blurb: A rock and mineral identifier for iOS. A photo gives you a shortlist; simple tests you run yourself narrow it down. When it is not sure, it says so instead of guessing.

bytebye.name: Bytebye
bytebye.blurb: A photo and video cleaner for iPhone and iPad. It finds duplicates, similar shots, screenshots, blurry photos and large videos, and shows how much space you would get back before you pay. The scan runs on your device and your photos go nowhere.

cleandev.name: CleanDev
cleandev.blurb: A developer cleanup tool for macOS. The Lite edition on the Mac App Store cleans the Flutter, Node and Unity project folders you choose. A full edition covering Xcode, simulators and package caches is coming soon. It explains what removing each item means and keeps what is still in use.

pulsewatch.name: PulseWatch
pulsewatch.blurb: Website change monitoring. It watches a page, or part of one, and alerts you by email, push, Slack, Discord or webhook when a price, stock level or listing changes. Available on the web and iOS.

snapslim.name: SnapSlim
snapslim.blurb: A file compression app for iPhone and iPad. It shrinks photos, videos and PDFs and creates and opens ZIP archives. Everything runs on the device; nothing is uploaded.

cleanlock.name: CleanLock
cleanlock.blurb: A keyboard and screen cleaning helper for Mac. While you wipe, it ignores keystrokes and trackpad clicks and covers every display. Afterwards you can test each key.

hesaplyor.name: hesaplyor.com
hesaplyor.blurb: Free, ad-supported calculators in Turkish and English. More than 60 tools, including VAT, salary, loans, currency, gold and BMI.

away-kingdom.name: Away Kingdom
away-kingdom.blurb: A digital-detox strategy game — the longer you stay away from your phone, the more resources you collect to grow your kingdom.

cevre-sikayet.name: Çevre Şikâyet
cevre-sikayet.blurb: An end-to-end municipal complaint platform that lets citizens report environmental issues with photo, location and a tracking code — developed and delivered by Akaya Labs.

patchkit.name: Patchkit
patchkit.blurb: SPF, DKIM and DMARC checks. It tests your domain's email authentication, explains each problem and its fix, and reads your DMARC reports to show who is sending mail as you. Available on the web and iOS.

kinetude.name: Kinetude
kinetude.blurb: A workout app and gym log for iPhone and iPad. It fits 121 training programs to your equipment, injuries and time, and shows 453 exercises muscle by muscle.

about.title: About Akaya Labs
about.intro: Akaya Labs is a one-person software studio founded by Ahmet Karaca in Rize, Türkiye, in 2026. It builds and publishes its own apps and takes on a few client projects a year. This page explains how it works and what it turns down.

vision.title: Few engagements done well. Growing the work, not the volume.
vision.lede: Akaya Labs aims to grow in the nature of its work — not in scale.

scale.heading: Not scale, substance
scale.body: Akaya Labs stays small on purpose. It takes a few client projects a year, which leaves enough time for those projects and for its own products. This limits revenue; in return, every project gets the direct attention of the person building it.

longevity.heading: The measure: still standing later
longevity.body: Akaya Labs was founded in 2026, so it cannot yet show what its products look like years on. The goal is plain: a product delivered today should still run well, and still be maintainable, three years from now. What can be shown today is the live products and the updates they receive.

partnership.heading: Few clients, long relationships
partnership.body: Akaya Labs does not work to a sales target. It aims for a working relationship with a few clients that continues after launch. Each project is planned so that the channel for maintenance and changes stays open.

discipline.heading: Disciplined growth
discipline.body: There is no intention of refusing growth, but the quality of the work comes first. Akaya Labs chooses to grow through more valuable and complex work rather than more of it. One day it may work with one or two senior collaborators; that would mean keeping the same discipline, not building departments.

mission.title: A precise, fast, premium development process that finishes the job.
mission.lede: Akaya Labs' promise to clients can be summarised in a single sentence: delivered on the date agreed, at the quality promised, without surprises.

precision.heading: Precise
precision.body: Every project starts, before any contract, with a written scope document that states what will and will not be built. Changes, extra costs and schedule shifts are approved in writing. Nothing is invoiced without that approval.

speed.heading: Fast
speed.body: The software industry tends to fail in two characteristic ways: at one end, half-finished MVPs shipped in two weeks; at the other, ambitious engagements that begin as 'six months' and stretch into a two-year scope creep. Akaya Labs stays away from both. We honour the timeline we committed to, and if it changes, the reason and the revised date are communicated together. For us, speed is not delivering quickly — it is keeping the word that was given.

premium.heading: Premium
premium.body: Performance, accessibility and security are decided at the start of a project, not added later. Code is kept clean and documented for a developer reading it two years after launch. The live products are the examples.

finished.heading: We finish what we start
finished.body: Akaya Labs does not ship a product and disappear. The channel stays open after launch for maintenance, scaling, new features and bug fixes. Through maintenance clauses or a retainer, the client keeps getting answers from the same developer.

discipline.heading: Disciplined
discipline.body: A studio's values show in the work it accepts. Akaya Labs does not design manipulative patterns, fabricated urgency, deceptive free-to-paid funnels or hidden subscriptions, and does not build software for gambling, betting or fraud-driven business models. These limits are raised openly in the first conversation and, where necessary, the project is declined.

manifesto.lede: Disciplined software. Delivery that keeps its word.
manifesto.p1: Akaya Labs is a one-person software studio. Interface design, frontend, server, mobile, infrastructure and post-launch support are all in the same hands. Nothing is lost between layers, and there is one person to ask. The cost is just as clear: only a few projects run at once.
manifesto.p2: We keep our distance from both extremes the software industry tends toward: the half-finished MVP rushed out in two weeks, and the ambitious engagement that stretches over two years and never actually ships. For Akaya Labs, the right pace is the pace at which a word can be kept. We honour the agreed timeline; when something needs to change, the reason and the revised schedule arrive together, and any additional cost is presented for client approval before an invoice is issued.
manifesto.p3: Akaya Labs takes a few projects a year, so that each one gets the time, attention and post-launch care it needs. This limits revenue. Time will show what it returns.
manifesto.p4: Akaya Labs does not design dark patterns or interfaces that manipulate the user, and does not build software for gambling, betting or fraud-driven business models. These limits are raised openly in the first conversation and, where required, the project is declined.

story.title: Akaya — calm, lasting and consistent.
story.p1: Our name carries both a sense of care and inherited memory. The gold ring on the logo — an enso from the sumi-e tradition — represents the beauty of the impermanent and a steady resolve drawn in a single stroke.
story.p2: The mountain silhouettes inside the ring are a nod to the Black Sea geography of Türkiye; quiet but rooted, making room for everything that grows on it. The sakura petal stands for softness; the crimson stamp for the accountability sitting beneath every product.
story.p3: Working with this palette is not coincidental. Like every Akaya Labs product, the brand identity is a slow, careful, and owned decision.

values.title: The values behind the work.
values.lede: Beyond brand identity, three core values shape how we work with clients.

team.title: One person, one point of accountability
team.body: Design decisions are made by the person who will write the code. The client always knows whom to ask. Illness or a full calendar are real risks in this structure, which is why schedules are written down and source code and access are documented and handed over to the client.

longterm.title: Long-term maintenance
longterm.body: The real life of a software product begins on the day it ships, not during delivery. Akaya Labs treats post-launch performance, maintenance, security updates and scaling as first-class concerns rather than optional add-ons. Post-launch maintenance is available through a project-based agreement or a retainer.

quality.title: Small studio, stated standards
quality.body: Performance, accessibility and security are discussed at the start of a project. Automated tests are standard on the backend; the client side is tested by hand on real devices. Code is written for the next developer reading it two years on, and architecture decisions are documented.

partnership.title: Partner, not vendor
partnership.body: Akaya Labs does not work like a vendor that finishes the design, sends an invoice and leaves; it also accounts for the long-term health of the product. Architecture choices, third-party dependencies and maintenance costs are discussed together, and the outcome is put in writing. Risks are raised before they materialise, not after.

scope.title: Written scope, no surprises
scope.body: Every project begins with an agreed, written scope document. It defines the technical requirements, the delivery schedule, the payment plan, the number of revisions included and what falls outside the project. Changes that emerge along the way are agreed in writing before they join the scope; any extra cost or time is presented for client approval before an invoice is issued.

communication.title: Right channel, fast response
communication.body: Client communication runs through a single official channel agreed at the start of the project. That channel, whether email, business messaging or a project management tool, stays the same throughout. Official matters receive a response within one or two business days; a separate fast channel can be defined for technical emergencies. The client always speaks with the same person through the same channel.

ownership.title: Ownership stays with the client
ownership.body: Once paid for, source code, design files and access keys belong to the client. User data belongs to the client from the start. If the client wants to continue with another developer, the handover runs cleanly, because architecture decisions, third-party dependencies and hidden configuration are documented from the outset. The Akaya Labs business model relies on clients choosing to continue, not on lock-in.

controller.heading: Data controller
controller.body: The data controller is Ahmet Karaca, trading as Akaya Labs (Rize, Türkiye). Contact: info@akayalabs.com. This notice is provided under Article 10 of Türkiye's Personal Data Protection Law No. 6698.

form.heading: Contact form
form.body: Data processed: your name, email address, subject, message and IP address. Purpose: to answer your request and prevent abuse of the form. Collection: electronically, when you submit the form. Legal basis: being directly related to forming a contract for project requests, and the controller's legitimate interest for other questions and abuse prevention (Article 5(2)(c) and (f)). Messages are delivered by email and kept as long as your request and legal obligations require. The IP address is held in memory for up to one hour to enforce a sending limit, and may also appear in the hosting provider's technical logs.

analytics.heading: Google Analytics
analytics.body: Loaded only if you accept in the cookie banner; if you decline or make no choice, it does not run. Data processed: online identifiers, pages visited, device and browser details. Purpose: to measure how the site is used. Collection: automatically, through cookies. Legal basis: your explicit consent (Article 5(1)). You can withdraw consent at any time with the button below, which also deletes the Analytics cookies.

cookies.heading: Cookies and browser storage
cookies.body: NEXT_LOCALE remembers your language and is needed for the site to work. cookie-consent stores your cookie choice in your browser. Cookies starting with _ga belong to Google Analytics and are written only with your consent.

transfer.heading: Recipients and transfers abroad
transfer.body: Your data is passed to these service providers: Google (email and, if you consent, Analytics) and Vercel (hosting and cookieless measurement). These companies' servers are abroad; your data may be transferred abroad, notably to the United States. The Analytics transfer relies on your explicit consent. Your data is not sold or used for advertising.

rights.heading: Your rights
rights.body: Under Article 11 of the law you may learn whether and how your data is processed and who receives it, request its correction or deletion, object to its processing and claim compensation for damage. Send requests to info@akayalabs.com; they are answered within 30 days at most. If you get no answer or find it inadequate, you may complain to Türkiye's Personal Data Protection Board. If you visit from the European Union, your GDPR rights remain unaffected.

measurement.heading: Cookieless measurement
measurement.body: Vercel Analytics and Speed Insights report page views and speed measurements in aggregate, without cookies. Purpose: to monitor how the site works and how fast it is. Legal basis: the controller's legitimate interest (Article 5(2)(f)).
